facts: The conditions during Race 2 were approximately 12–14 knots of wind and 0.3 m waves.
GBR 315 and GER 289 were sailing on starboard tack from mark 1 to mark 1a to be left on port.
GBR 315 reached the zone one boat length clear ahead of GER 289.
After entering the zone, GBR 315 bore away towards the mark.
Before GBR 315 had left the mark astern, GER 289 sailed between GBR 315 and the mark.
GER 289’s position prevented GBR 315 from sailing directly to the mark.
Contact occurred between the transom of GBR 315 and the bow of GER 289.
There was no damage or injury.
conclusions: When GBR 315 reached the zone of mark 1a clear ahead, she became entitled to mark-room under rule RRS 18.2(b).
GER 289 failed to give GBR 315 mark-room and broke rule RRS 18.2(b).
It was reasonably possible for GER 289 to avoid contact; therefore she broke rule RRS 14 (a).

It was not reasonably possible for GBR 315 the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact when it became clear that GER 289 was not giving mark-room. GBR 315 did not break RRS 14(b).

GBR 315 to windward failed to keep clear of GER 289 to leeward, and broke RRS 11. Since GBR 315 broke RRS 11 while she was sailing within the [mark-room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.
decision: GER 289 is DSQ in Race 2 for breaking Rules RRS 18.2(b) and RRS 14(a).
